service.name: Live music for a backyard party
service.serviceType: A singer with a guitar, a jazz duo, a flamenco trio, a party band or a DJ for backyard and summer parties at home
service.description: Live music for a backyard party across Denver and the Front Range: a singer with a guitar or a jazz duo on the patio at 65 to 72 dBA, a flamenco trio for a summer evening, a trio or quartet on the lawn for the part of the night that dances, and a DJ once the loud part moves indoors, with sound support sized to the yard, cover and power settled before the day, and one personal contact for the night.

faqs.q: Can we hire a band for a backyard party?
faqs.a: Yes. A yard books three sizes: a singer with a guitar or a jazz duo on the patio at a volume the tables talk across, a trio or a quartet on the lawn for the part of the night that dances, and a DJ once the loud part moves indoors. It's one contract with one personal contact, and sound support that's the right size for a yard is included.

faqs.q: What does a band for a backyard party cost?
faqs.a: The pricing page sets out what live music costs in this market, and the cost guide has the Colorado figures for each kind of night, house parties included. A yard books one size for the afternoon and another for the evening, so send the date and a sentence about the yard and we'll come back with a configuration and a price for the whole party.

faqs.q: Does the band need power in the backyard?
faqs.a: Yes, one dedicated circuit for a solo, a duo, a trio or a DJ and two for a quartet, and a wall socket through the nearest window is the answer that beats any generator. A generator works if it's a quiet one, properly grounded and sized with headroom above what the band draws; a domestic generator at the edge of the lawn isn't that, and its noise sits underneath every quiet moment. Where there's no socket at all, a guitarist can play with a battery-powered system.

faqs.q: What if it rains, or gets cold?
faqs.a: The band and the sound desk need cover in any forecast, a patio roof, a pergola with a top on it or a tent, because Colorado evenings cool fast enough that by the end of a damp night the musicians are retuning between songs. If there's a move-indoors plan, it needs a decision time and a person named to make the call, and the main floor or the garage should be ready to take the smaller setup.

faqs.q: How late can a band play in a backyard in Denver?
faqs.a: The loud part of an outdoor party has a short life anywhere in the city, and the later the hour the shorter it gets, so we put the band on the patio while the sun is up and move the loud part indoors or to the DJ when it goes down. The rules vary by street and by HOA, so we don't quote an ordinance; if yours has a number in writing, give it to us at contract and the night gets built under it.

faqs.q: How much space does the band need on a patio or a lawn?
faqs.a: A singer with a guitar or a DJ takes 6 by 4 feet, a duo 8 by 6, a trio 12 by 8 and a quartet 14 by 10, all under cover. Load-in runs 45 minutes for a solo or a DJ, an hour for a duo or a trio and 90 minutes for a quartet, and on a yard that means telling us which gate or side path is ours.

faqs.q: Can the same band play the afternoon and the evening?
faqs.a: Yes. A backyard party is an afternoon that turns into an evening, and one booking covers both: a singer with a guitar or a duo while the food is on, at 65 to 72 dBA at the nearest table, and the band or the DJ once the light goes. Sets run 45 to 60 minutes with music through the breaks, so the yard never goes quiet.

faqs.q: Which Saturdays go first in the summer?
faqs.a: The Saturdays in June and September are the ones every wedding in the state wants too, so a summer Saturday is the date to send early. A Sunday afternoon, a Friday evening or a weeknight in July is the easier ask.
